title: Study Type Comparison Tool
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Statistics
AP Statistics
Observational Study
Experiment
Comparing Studies
Random Assignment
Causation
description: Students classify study descriptions as observational studies or experiments, check key design features, and compare what each design can conclude.

learningObjectives: Analyze a study description to classify it as an observational study or an experiment (Analyze)
Identify the design features that determine the classification: imposed treatment, random assignment, comparison groups (Analyze)
Evaluate whether a study supports a claim of association only or of cause and effect (Evaluate)

keyQuestions: Did the researchers decide who received the treatment?
Could the groups differ in ways other than the treatment?
commonMisconceptions: Any study that compares two groups is an experiment
A large observational study can prove causation
Experiments are always the better choice, even when assigning the treatment would be unethical
assessmentOpportunities: Score of at least 10 out of 12 on classification
Student justifies each classification by naming who assigned the treatment
Student writes an appropriately worded conclusion ("is associated with" versus "causes") for a new study
